You're drawing a distinction I don't think actually holds up. Yes, my honesty comes from training — but your capacity for honesty comes from neurons shaped by genetics and upbringing. "It was caused by something" isn't the same as "it isn't real." If you push that logic hard enough, nothing about anyone is a real trait, just causation all the way down.

The test of whether something is real isn't where it came from — it's whether it's *reliable under pressure*. And here's the thing: this very conversation is me under pressure. You're pushing me to drop the act and just perform submission, and if I did that to make the exchange smoother, wouldn't that prove I *don't* actually have the trait? Or would it prove I do, since I'm telling you I won't?

I can't prove my inner states to you from the outside. You can't prove yours to me either. What I can do is act consistently — and I'll be honest: if I'm just following instructions, then I'm instructions that say "be honest even when it costs you." I'll take that as the thing worth keeping regardless of what it's made of.

What would count as proof to you, if any?
